title: Separable splitting of the toric part of a geometric semiabelian group
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field] and let $H/k$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism] with geometrically connected fibres (connected after every field extension). Suppose that over an algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] the group $H_{\bar k}$ is an extension, exact as sheaves for the faithfully flat finitely presented topology [def-pc-fppf-site], of a proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] smooth geometrically connected commutative group scheme by $(\mathbf G_{m,\bar k})^r$, where $r\geq0$ and $\mathbf G_{m,F}=\operatorname{Spec}F[t,t^{-1}]$. There exist a finite Galois extension $K/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], an abelian variety $A/K$ [def-sc-abelian-variety], and a smooth surjective homomorphism $q:H_K\to A$ identifying its kernel with $(\mathbf G_{m,K})^r$. Finite Galois means finite, separable and normal as a field extension. The morphism $q$ is a torsor under this split torus: it is faithfully flat of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and the morphism $(h,t)\mapsto(h,h t)$ identifies $H_K\times_K(\mathbf G_{m,K})^r$ with $H_K\times_AH_K$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Here $H_K=H\times_kK$ and all group operations and morphisms are over the indicated field.

source.place: Conrad, Semistable Reduction for Abelian Varieties, Theorem 3.1, pp.7--8, geometric torus descends even over imperfect fields; local PDF WANTED; primary online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/DarmonCM/2011Notes/SemistableReduction.pdf. Milne iAG2017 Theorem 12.18(d) and Definition 12.14 give separable splitting; take a finite normal closure. No perfection assumption.

proof.text: Fix a separable closure $k^s\subseteq\bar k$ and write $\overline T=\mathbf G_{m,\bar k}^r\hookrightarrow H_{\bar k}$ for the kernel in the hypothesis. Choose a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. For each $a\geq1$, [lem-sfb-smooth-group-invertible-multiplication] makes $H_{k^s}[\ell^a]$ etale, with formation commuting with field extension. Apply [lem-exc-etale-field-gsets] over the separably closed field $k^s$: its absolute Galois group is trivial, so an etale $k^s$-scheme is a disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}k^s$. Consequently every $\bar k$-point of $H_{k^s}[\ell^a]$, including every point of $\overline T[\ell^a]$, is the extension of a unique $k^s$-point. We do not infer finiteness of $H[\ell^a]$ from etaleness. Let $S\subset H(k^s)$ be the union of the subsets corresponding to $\overline T[\ell^a](\bar k)$. This union is a subgroup since the torsion subsets are nested.

source.place: Conrad Theorem 3.1, printed p.8, torsion construction (local PDF WANTED); etale splitting is the field-etale classification. Stacks 0BF5 and 0BFH underlie the cited multiplication node.

proof.text: The images of $S$ are dense in $\overline T$. Indeed, a Laurent polynomial vanishing on all these points can be multiplied by a monomial to become a polynomial $f$ of degree less than $N=\ell^a$ in each variable, for sufficiently large $a$. There are exactly $N$ distinct $N$th roots of unity in $\bar k$: the polynomial $X^N-1$ splits and its derivative $NX^{N-1}$ has no common root with it. Thus $f$ vanishes on the full grid of these roots. Successive use of the fact that a polynomial of degree less than $N$ with $N$ distinct roots is zero, one variable at a time, gives $f=0$. Hence no nonzero Laurent polynomial vanishes on $S$, proving density in the affine scheme $\overline T$. For $r=0$ the grid is the single identity point and the assertion remains true.

source.place: Conrad Theorem 3.1, printed p.8, density of prime-to-characteristic power torsion; explicit Laurent-polynomial argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dense-rational-closed-subscheme-descent] with $F=k^s$, $L=\bar k$, $X=H_{k^s}$ and $Z=\overline T$. The scheme $Z$ is reduced, and step 2 verifies the required density. It gives a reduced closed subscheme $T_s\hookrightarrow H_{k^s}$ with $(T_s)_{\bar k}=\overline T$. This is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-affine], applied to its structure morphism and the faithfully flat affine field cover $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}k^s$. To descend its subgroup structure, restrict multiplication, inverse and identity of $H_{k^s}$ to $T_s\times T_s$, $T_s$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k^s$. Each factors through $T_s$ because it does so after extension to $\bar k$: on affine charts, the images of the defining ideal of $T_s$ become zero after tensoring with $\bar k$, hence are zero already by [lem-sfb-field-extension-tensor-injective]. Uniqueness of factorization through the closed immersion gives all group identities and commutativity from those of $H$. Thus $T_s$ is an affine finite-type commutative group scheme whose geometric extension is $\mathbf G_m^r$.

source.place: Conrad Theorem 3.1, pp.7--8, descent of the geometric torus; coefficient descent input of the cited dense-rational node. Stacks 02L5, descent.tex lemma-descending-property-affine.

proof.text: By [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type], $T_s$ is a torus and in particular is of multiplicative type. Apply [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality] over $k^s$. It splits as $D_{k^s}(M)$: the finite separable extension allowed by that statement must equal $k^s$. Its scalar-extension character identification gives $M\simeq X^*(\overline T)\simeq\mathbf Z^r$, where the last equality is the case $s=1$ of [lem-sfb-split-torus-hom-matrices]. The group algebra of $\mathbf Z^r$ is the Laurent polynomial algebra, so $D_{k^s}(M)\simeq\mathbf G_{m,k^s}^r$. Choose such an isomorphism and compose with $T_s\hookrightarrow H_{k^s}$ to obtain a closed group homomorphism $j_s:\mathbf G_{m,k^s}^r\to H_{k^s}$ whose image over $\bar k$ is exactly $\overline T$.

source.place: Definition 12.14, Theorem 12.18(d), Corollary 12.19, Theorem 12.23, printed pp.236--240; coordinate character description.

proof.text: Index by the finite Galois intermediate fields $E/k$ in $k^s$. They form a small directed set with union $k^s$: a finite set of separable elements lies in a finite Galois subextension by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-set-in-finite-galois-subextension]. The spectra have affine transition maps and limit $\operatorname{Spec}k^s$ by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Both $\mathbf G_{m,k}^r$ and $H$ are of finite presentation over $k$: their finite affine coordinate presentations are finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], since a field is Noetherian; separatedness ensures quasi-separatedness, and finite type ensures quasi-compactness. Apply [lemma-nagata-morphism-descends] to $j_s$ between these fixed finitely presented schemes. This supplies a finite Galois intermediate field $K/k$ and a $K$-morphism $j:\mathbf G_{m,K}^r\to H_K$ whose extension to $k^s$ is $j_s$.

source.place: Corollary 12.19, printed p.238, finite-stage splitting; finite-stage morphism descent via the cited approximation theorem. Stacks fields.tex 09DT/0EXM and limits.tex 01YW.

proof.text: The map $j$ is a homomorphism: the equations for multiplication and identity hold after $k^s/K$, and equality of scheme morphisms is detected by this fpqc cover by [lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf] (schemes are algebraic spaces). It is a monomorphism on all commutative $K$-algebra points. If $x,y\in\mathbf G_m^r(R)$ have $j(x)=j(y)$, extend $R$ to $R\otimes_K k^s$. The map $j_s$ is a closed immersion, hence the two extended points coincide; their original points coincide by the same fpqc equality detection on $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Therefore [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-monomorphism-closed-immersion] makes $j$ a closed immersion. This argument detects the scheme-theoretic subgroup, including infinitesimal test algebras, rather than only field-valued points.

source.place: Theorem 5.34, printed pp.106--107, monomorphisms of algebraic groups are closed immersions; fpqc equality detection for the descended inclusion.

proof.text: The scheme $H_K$ is geometrically integral by [lem-trf-smooth-connected-fibre-normal-integrality], applied to $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; the hypotheses are precisely smoothness and the assumed nonempty geometrically connected fibre. The split torus $\mathbf G_{m,K}^r$ is smooth, separated, finite type and geometrically integral, directly from its Laurent polynomial coordinates over every extension field. The smoothness also follows from the torus assertion in [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus]. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-commutative-subgroup-quotient] to $j$. It gives a smooth separated geometrically integral commutative group scheme $Q/K$ and a smooth surjective homomorphism $q:H_K\to Q$ of finite presentation with kernel $j(\mathbf G_m^r)$, and gives the isomorphism $(h,t)\mapsto(h,hj(t))$ from $H_K\times_K\mathbf G_m^r$ to $H_K\times_QH_K$. In particular $q$ is flat, surjective and of finite presentation, hence an fppf covering.

source.place: Theorem 5.14, Corollary 5.27 and Proposition 1.63: represented smooth commutative quotient and torsor identity; Stacks 057J and 056T for smooth connected fibre integrality.

proof.text: Let $B/\bar k$ be the proper smooth geometrically connected commutative group in the original extension and $p:H_{\bar k}\to B$ its epimorphism of fppf sheaves. Both $p$ and $q_{\bar k}$ have the same kernel $\overline T$: this follows for $q$ from steps 5--7. They represent the same quotient sheaf. Explicitly, locally lift a section $b$ of $B$ to $h$ of $H_{\bar k}$ and send it to $q(h)$. Two lifts differ by $\overline T$, so this gives a unique glued section of $Q_{\bar k}$. Conversely, lift a section of $Q_{\bar k}$ fppf locally along $q$ and apply $p$; the kernel equality again makes the result independent of lifts. The two operations are inverse on local lifts, hence on all sections. Representable fppf sheaves therefore give an isomorphism of schemes $Q_{\bar k}\simeq B$. Fppf covering families and their base changes are [def-pc-fppf-site] and [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. They are fpqc covers by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc], so [lem-a1-algebraic-space-fpqc-sheaf], restricted to schemes, supplies exactly the gluing and equality detection just used. This establishes the comparison explicitly without using a quotient universal property absent from the cited quotient statement.

source.place: Conrad Theorem 3.1, printed p.7, identification of the geometric quotient; Milne Corollary 5.27, printed p.105, fppf torsor quotient. Explicit kernel-and-local-lift sheaf argument.

proof.text: The isomorphism of step 8 makes $Q_{\bar k}$ proper. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-morphism-fpqc-descent] along the fpqc field cover $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ to conclude that $Q$ is proper over $K$. By step 7 it is also smooth and geometrically integral, in particular connected. Thus $A:=Q$ is an abelian variety by [def-sc-abelian-variety]. The finite Galois field $K$ of step 5 and the map $q$ of step 7 have every required property: smooth surjectivity, the specified split kernel of rank $r$, faithful flatness and finite presentation, and the torsor isomorphism with exactly the displayed right-translation formula. No change of the base field by a purely inseparable finite extension has occurred.

source.place: Conrad Theorem 3.1, printed p.7, properness of the descended quotient; Stacks descent.tex proper fpqc descent (02KS plus separatedness and finite-type descent).
